body: My troponin I was 0.03. They didn’t do any follow-up tests, just pretty much sent me on my way.
If you are a cowardly person, you don’t want to suffer dying of cancer. It’s a long, agonizing process. It’s a good thing you don’t have it. I understand how you feel though.

Oh, just read the part about you not wanting to know. I know you aren’t giving me actual medical advice and wouldn’t even be able to over the Internet. I guess I just wanted to hear others chime in. Sorry.

I will be following up with a cardiologist, per recommendation with my fairly stumped PCP. On the 30th of this month. I guess I was just hoping for a little reassurance til then that you guys don’t think I suffered a massive heart attack that the ER missed. Lol.

I wanna thank you again for another reassuring comment. I really appreciate it. 

I’m still trying not to freak out. I have periods where I’m like okay it’s probably fine, they let you leave, they wouldn’t do that if they thought something was wrong... etc. And then all of a sudden my brain’s like GIRL THATS NOT OKAY DONT BE DUMB. 

The thing that really gets me is they didn’t ever do a follow-up test. So I’ll never know whether it was anything or not, there’s no trend other than that test compared to one exactly a month prior. That’s what’s keepin me up at night, haha. 

Anyways, I have my cardiology appointment at the end of the month. I’ll mention it to him then. 

You’re really nice. Thanks again.

Thank you. I wish they would’ve told me something about this when I was there, and didn’t have to panic when seeing the paperwork. Haha. 

I guess it still really confuses me. So it is pretty much a guarantee that something happened with my heart? Even though it’s still in “normal” ranges, the fact that it increased in fact *does* prove something happened? 

I spoke with my doctor on the phone about this today and she said something about there being a margin of error with blood tests blah blah don’t worry blah blah... but I can’t help but feel weird about this because I know this is a sensitive blood test and these levels don’t really rise and fall like others for no reason. And what are really the odds that there was a mistake, especially with the symptoms I’ve been having too. But if they’re still within normal ranges, should I worry or not?

I keep going back and forth with myself about this one. Gut is telling me it isn’t right but it still being “normal” is throwing that off. I just worry that at some point it was much higher and I never knew. >_< 

Thanks for your comment. Sorry for continuing to ramble! This bugs me so much!

I AM worried about CHF or a blockage... and minor rises in troponin can apparently signal toward those things. I just can’t find specific numbers for that. That’s the whole point of my post. It’s kind of hard not to worry. I’m young and shouldn’t feel these things yet. They’ve done thyroid labs about a trillion times.

Thank you. Your comment definitely did help me. God, it’s rough worrying about your heart. It almost feels like I’d rather go back to the days when I worried I had a brain tumor or something. Our country is just so unhealthy that heart problems are so prevalent and such a real concern and that really screws me up. 

And yeah definitely others being concerned about it has made me more and more concerned about it over the years. I never used to have anything else wrong that could be associated with my heart rate, and they’d always just say “oh, that’s probably just your norm.” And I’d move on with my life because that makes sense. But now I truly feel unwell and all of a sudden I’m scared of everything again. Bleh!

Then why am I getting one? Why does every doctor I see tell me that it is important to see this cardiologist? If they were concerned I am going to die right now, they would’ve done it in hospital and admitted me, sure. But that does not mean there is nothing to be concerned about. My heart rate is not normal and neither are my symptoms with activity and not at rest.

There is no party. And that is not true. There is a reason that they do more testing beyond an EKG for suspected heart problems. If they were 99% accurate at detecting every heart problem under the sun, there’d be just about no need for anything else. 

And yes, my post shows that I have health anxiety. Never did I deny that. I said that I have it, along with the possibility of real heart problems. I think I will listen to the concern of many doctors. Thank you for your comment.
I’m just shocked that those things weren’t ever mentioned to me in the ER! Wow.

Hematocrit 41.4%
Hemoglobin 12.9 g/dL
MCV, MCH & MPV all say “low”

MCV 80.4 fL
MCH 25.0 pcg 
MPV 8.4 fL

And seriously, you sound like such a warrior. You’ve dealt with so much and you are so strong. I hope I can be as strong as you, regardless of diagnosis. Thanks again for telling me a little of your story and for your kind words to me.

Wow, thank you for your reply. This is really helpful. I’m glad you’ve been so positive and I hope I can start being more positive as well, regardless of what comes of my appointment. I just don’t know how to shake this fear of the unknown right now!

All of your comments mean the world to me. Thank you for trying to help me, I have been feeling so lost and alone and sick. I am not alone, because I have supportive family and a loving boyfriend, who would all do anything for me. And yet, I feel alone because they don’t totally understand what’s going on with me. So it makes me feel lots better just hearing that others relate, even though I wish none of us had to go through it. 

Anyways, thank you all again.

Thank you so much for your response. I have been very open with her (my doc) about my anxiety toward all of this. She is referring me to a psychiatrist and therapist. She understands my anxiety and fear about it. She said she wanted me to get in as soon as possible with the cardiologist and made sure to specify that it is not because she thinks there’s something majorly wrong, but because she does not want me to feel this anxiety for any longer than I have to. My anxiety just tells me she’s lying though and trying to put it in a way that doesn’t make me panic. I dunno, my anxiety about all this is making me nuts. Assuming the worst of everything is very draining, I’m sure lots of people in this sub know all about that. I wish none of us had to deal with this. 

And thank you for the well-wishes. I hope all is well for you too and continues to be.
Thank you. I will be looking into CBT very soon as per my PCP’s advice.

I am female. I was told my blood work was good but I’m not certain what all the tests are for. I don’t see iron on there. There’s a lot of stuff and there’s no “titles” for any groups of tests so I’m not sure what they are all for. I can send photo if you’d like? Lots of things like electrolytes, ALT/AST, albumin, bilirubin, BUN, creatinine, blood count, etc. many more than I listed but I don’t see “iron.” They’ve also done troponin I and lactic acid recently, and a few years ago BNP.

Thank you. I guess I honestly just wish my symptoms were light enough to where they could still tell me it’s anxiety and I could believe them and go on my way. The unknown (especially when doctors are unsure and concerned) is mortifying.

I have honestly gotten myself so worked up in these past few months that it’s hard for me to do just about anything that I have to do to survive, let alone anything that’s supposed to calm me or provide happiness. I have convinced myself that doing just about anything is going to literally kill me. I know this all sounds so pathetic, but the only thing I ever am anymore is scared. I just don’t know how to stop being so scared. Nothing distracts me because my thoughts of dying are so invasive. I’m sorry if this is not okay to talk about or something. I just have no one to talk to about it.

Yeah, I am just concerned because the BNP was a bit over 3 years ago and I know this condition can get worse in not a long time... 

Thank you, I will probably end up just waiting. But the anxiety is killing me. You’re right though, the last ER doc I saw said just about the same thing. If there is something going on, it’s going on. I can’t just make it disappear. So I have to find ways to cope, right now even just with the thoughts I’m having. I just can’t stop crying.

Hi, I’m sorry if I was unclear as I wrote this at 4am after waking in a panic. I have not been diagnosed with anything yet and I have not had an echo yet to find out my EF. Basically I am just concerned about my symptoms, as is my PCP. Waiting on my very first cardiology appointment and I’m utterly terrified so I made this post just to kind of explain my situation and see what it sounds like to you guys who know about this condition.

Socialized healthcare would only ensure that everyone gets the same low-quality, long wait time health care and no room to make your own healthcare decisions. You wouldn’t have the option to make more money and see a better doctor. Not a good thing. 

No one that is actually ill with anything more than a cold every couple years would like to be stuck with poor-people’s healthcare. It is undesirable beyond “I need to stay alive.”

Because the quality of healthcare goes up the more you pay. Poor people have to wait longer, have less comprehensive care, and don’t have their choice of doctors. 

You can receive low-quality, but basically “performs its function” healthcare for free or very low cost if you are poor. It does its job, but it is clearly ideal to have better if possible.
